analysis.title: Global Majors & E&P Comparative Valuations
key_insights: Global Majors trade at 5.8x EV/DACF (enterprise value over debt-adjusted cash flow) in 2026E and 6.2x in 2027E under futures pricing. North American Majors are at 6.8x and 7.1x, European Majors at 4.2x and 4.9x.
European Majors continue to trade at a discount to North American Majors in both 2026E and 2027E under futures pricing.
North American Senior E&Ps trade at 6.4x EV/DACF in 2026E and 5.2x in 2027E, above Intermediate E&Ps (5.4x and 4.6x) in both years. Canadian Seniors are at 6.0x and 6.2x, US Seniors at 6.6x and 4.7x.
Canadian Intermediate E&Ps trade above their US counterparts in both years: 6.3x and 5.5x against 3.7x and 3.1x. International E&P is the cheapest group at 2.7x and 2.3x.

Futures strip: Brent $93.89/bbl in 2026E falling to $82.20 in 2027E, WTI $86.33 falling to $76.22, Henry Hub $3.56 falling to $3.05/mmBtu. Brokers (Bloomberg consensus) are at Brent $94.11 and $80.80 and Henry Hub $3.28 in both years.
The Brent-WTI spread is $7.56 in 2026E and $5.98 in 2027E on futures, against a consensus 2027E spread of $2.80. The WTI-WCS differential widens from $16.76 to $19.89 on futures.

Rating and implied-return spread within the majors: Imperial Oil is the only Underperform at C$138 target (-19% implied return). BP (30%), Canadian Natural (39%) and Cenovus (38%) carry the highest implied returns among the integrated names.
Among Senior E&Ps, Expand Energy has the highest implied return (58%, $131 target), followed by Diamondback (40%, $240) and Whitecap (40%, C$22). All three are Outperform.

Among US Intermediates, California Resources (76%, $77 target) and Infinity Natural Resources (68%, $21) have the highest implied returns. Both are Outperform. Free cash flow yields are 17% for the US Intermediate group average in 2026E.
Free cash flow is negative or near zero for several small Canadian names in 2026E, including Paramount (-$392M), Spartan Delta (-$173M), Obsidian (-$55M) and Coelacanth (-$31M).

International E&P: Parex trades at 1.9x price to EPS and 1.8x EV/DACF in 2026E with a 7.9% dividend yield. Aker BP (8.3% yield) and Var Energi (9.7% yield) carry the highest dividend yields in the table.

Devon, EQT, Ovintiv, Range, Greenfire, Logan and Strathcona are marked Restricted, so no rating, target or estimates are shown. Prices are as of November 18, 2026, and ratings and targets use RBC's base commodity deck.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Futures price a $11.69/bbl decline in Brent from 2026E to 2027E. This is the deck used for the futures-pricing valuations.
Consensus is slightly above futures in 2026E and slightly below in 2027E.
Consensus spread is $8.81 in 2026E and $2.80 in 2027E, so brokers expect a much narrower 2027E spread than futures.
European gas is priced at a large premium to Henry Hub in both years.
The Canadian heavy oil discount widens in 2027E on futures.
Canadian gas prices are priced lower in 2027E.
Refining margins are priced lower in 2027E.
